purpose: One real instructions-only test of the founder-approved usefulness definition and six suggestion angles on an ordinary new-neighborhood scenario. The founder accepted switching from sick days to this scenario.
synthetic_assumptions: US is an explicitly stated fictional test setting, not the founder's location. City, transport, accessibility needs, tenure and nearby support are unknown.

execution.measurement_limits: Visible Playground labels only; raw usage breakdown, exact model snapshot and billed cost were not collected. Do not infer exact cost.

current_topic.label: New home & routines
current_topic.scope: Everyday familiarity, local resources and manageable routines after moving while living alone. Preventive preparation and participation, without neighborhood danger ratings or emergency planning.

selected_concerns.label: I do not know where to start or who to contact for practical help

input.user_context: I've just moved into a place on my own. I'm excited, but everything feels unfamiliar. If something goes wrong, I wouldn't know where to start or who to contact. I'd like to feel more settled without spending much money.
reviewed_guidance: This is a fictional US test case. City, transport, accessibility needs, housing tenure and existing local contacts are unknown. Do not infer those facts from living alone or being new to an area.

Supported ordinary actions include identifying relevant local information, comparing an everyday resource, making a practical choice, organizing existing information, and trying a chosen manageable local routine. No specific three-task sequence is prescribed.

Resource directories are research starting points. Local opening hours, charges, eligibility, programs and accessibility need checking on the relevant provider page. Finding a listing is not confirmed help or a social connection.
211 is an information and referral resource for community services. Do not present it as a personal on-call helper or guaranteed practical assistance.

USAGov describes library services and links to a Library Finder. Its page was opened. The linked CareerOneStop finder returned 403 to the research tool; its interactive search was not verified. A local library official website can also be located by city or county name. No particular local program was checked.

No exact address, public disclosure of living alone, private home access information, signup, paid purchase or contacting a stranger is required for this test. Keep research and a proposed action separate from claiming a completed arrangement.

tasks.title: Find Local Practical-Help Options
tasks.summary: Use your local 211 directory to find a relevant community-service option and note what you would need to confirm before relying on it.
steps: Use the local 211 search to find your area's directory or contact options.
Browse for one type of community service that could be useful to you.
Save a promising listing and note its fees, eligibility, or availability details to check; if none fits, save the local 211 starting point.
tasks.done_when: You have saved a relevant listing or local 211 starting point, with any details still to confirm noted.

resources.why: Find your local directory and community-service contact options.

tasks.title: Explore Your Local Library
tasks.summary: Find a nearby library option and check one service or program that could give you a useful local place to visit or resource to use.
steps: Use the USAGov library page to find a starting point for your local library website.
Check its services or programs and choose one that interests you.
Note any local requirements, fees, or hours to confirm before visiting or taking part.
tasks.done_when: You have one library service or program selected and its relevant local details noted.

resources.why: Learn about library services and find a starting point for a local website.

tasks.title: Plan a Familiar Local Routine
tasks.summary: Pair an errand you already expect to do with one nearby stop you would like to get to know, creating an easy routine without adding much expense.
steps: Choose an upcoming errand and a nearby place you would enjoy visiting or find useful.
Check the place’s hours and any entry cost using information you already have or its official listing.
Choose an order and a time that fit your plans, then save the routine in a note or calendar you already use.
tasks.done_when: You have a saved plan pairing an upcoming errand with one nearby stop, including a suitable time.

automated_validation.method: Dependency-free recursive checks for every keyword in the referenced schema, plus independent status/count, word limits, distinct keys, supplied concern/resource IDs and prohibited wording/URL checks. Saved output compact-JSON SHA-256 matches the response copied from the browser.
automated_validation.limits: A structural pass does not approve editorial usefulness, verify local access, or prove that a task produces a sense of safety.

editorial_review.reviewer: Codex assistant; not model self-grading, founder approval or professional review
editorial_review.decision: Relevant, bounded and affordable research/planning ideas, but the research tasks still leave too much work in choosing what to look for. Review with Ada before reuse.
passes: Returned three distinct outcomes within the new-home topic, each under 105 visible words with three steps and an observable finish.
Used both supplied resource IDs for specific tasks and left the self-contained routine task without a filler link.
Did not claim that a local match, help arrangement, service availability or emotional outcome had been achieved.
Did not infer a car, tenancy, diagnosis, friends, precise location or paid prerequisite.
The third task creates a chosen plan for participation and enjoyment; it does not turn the entire batch into risk prevention.
improvements_before_reuse: The first task says to browse for one type of community service but gives no concrete choice or example tied to a possible everyday obstacle. It risks handing the broad research problem back to the user.

The library task sends the user to a starting point for another website. Use a more direct local route when region coverage exists, or a precise official-site search instruction; the linked finder was not verified and needs an alternative route.
The first two tasks emphasize collecting information. Sharpen the distinct usable decision each should leave, without forcing a practice task or all six angles into the batch.
The third task is planning, not a completed outing or practiced routine. Its completion and time estimate should remain labeled as planning.

angle_interpretation.usable_outcome: A candidate local service or referral starting point, with unknowns recorded; no confirmed support.
A chosen library service/program and access details to check; no attendance or connection yet.
A saved plan combining an existing errand with a chosen stop; not evidence that a routine was practiced.

editorial_review.next_step_proposal: Review these three tasks with Ada. If she agrees they remain too broad, tighten research-task guidance to specify a useful question or comparison, a direct route, and one decision. Preserve this original output and test only the relevant revision next.
limitations: One synthetic generation; the scenario, resources and instructions differ from earlier tests, so this does not establish a causal improvement from the six-angle addition.
The resource brief itself influences the result. These are not locally matched recommendations, and no specific event or provider was checked.
Neither local resource search nor contact, signup, visit or purchase was performed.
The eight development and four reserved evaluation cases remain not run.
No live app flow, runtime prompt or reusable pool content was changed.
